candidates.loopsAndStops: Five loops, five hard integer caps, no loop whose exit depends on a subjective "until it is good". L1 clarifying questions: one round, at most two questions, each with a recommended default so silence is an answer; on stop, proceed on the defaults and record them as assumptions. L2 direction veto: fires when ledger.mjs check returns a collision; cap two vetoes; on stop the run halts and reports the collision and the two theses tried, and does not try a third. L3 build/edit: fires when verify.mjs --no-axe reports a defect on the changed surface; cap two attempts on the same defect; on stop report it unresolved and move on, where it reappears at L4. L4 inspection: two rounds maximum, each opening with the single word ship, fix or rebuild, and a rebuild round applies no fixes (impeccable/bounded-finish-review-loop); on stop, whatever is still wrong goes into PRODUCTION-REPORT.md and the loop ends. L5 release: fires when any of the four release commands fails; cap two reruns; on stop write the failure into the report, and never edit a check to make it pass. The run always terminates in a written report rather than in a question.

candidates.howItAvoidsHouseStyle: Four devices, and the candidate states plainly which two are enforcement and which two are persuasion. Persuasion: (1) the generative rule diverges by construction — "derive from THIS subject's world" has a different answer for a tannery, a tide clock and a seed library, with the operational form being "concrete nouns, not adjectives", because adjectives are category-level and every category produces the same ones; (2) section 4 names our OWN measured recipe — uppercase mono labels, hairline separators, tabular figures as motif, flat surfaces — alongside frontend-design's three clusters, all named and none banned per C1, with the explicit rule that the only forbidden thing is arriving somewhere without choosing it. Enforcement: (3) gate.mjs collects every --custom-property name declared in the build's CSS and fails if ≥80% come from a fixed generic vocabulary (bg, surface, fg, text, muted, border, accent, primary, secondary, card, ring, input, destructive, radius, shadow). This is the NORDRIG-AB-FORENSICS section 1 finding — once a variable is called --caution the world has already answered where it goes, whereas --accent forces every later decision to be made from zero and zero has a house style — and nothing in v2.3 checks it. It costs ~30 lines and it attacks convergence BEFORE the render. It does not decide anything; it refuses a build that never made a decision. (4) ledger.mjs fingerprints the finished render on six fields against a hard-coded round-8 recipe that fails even on an empty ledger, the dark-ground/one-saturated-accent monoculture from PALETTE-ANALYSIS finding 4, and an append-only ~/.sitesmith/renders.jsonl that stores no client URL. History may veto, never propose (C7) — there is no path by which a stored fingerprint becomes an input to a new design. Set-level diversity (ledger.mjs --set) runs only for A9 and the showcase, never during a customer build, because a single site cannot be measured for a property that only exists across a set.
candidates.howItIsTested: Test 0, first and cheapest: the re-expression smoke test, which is the charter's own open risk:reexpression-may-not-transfer. Same brief, same model, our SKILL.md sections 1-7 versus the upstream 55-line frontend-design file, blind-scored by two reviewers on the existing rubric. If our re-expression scores below the original, this candidate's premise is dead and no production layer rescues it. One brief, two builds. Run it before anything else is built. CI gates: tools/check-repo.py enforces SKILL.md under 500 lines (measured 242), hash-matched licence texts and notices, plus a NEW string scan for text traceable to website-builder-setup or redesign-skill because C-no-unlicensed-text bans close paraphrase and file-presence cannot check that; tools/context-budget.mjs gates ALWAYS ≤ 3,300 and ROUTINE ≤ 6,000 est tokens and fails CI on either, because a budget without a gate is a note; verify.mjs against benchmarks/06-redesign/before/ must still exit non-zero and CI fails if the control group passes (C-control-group). Fixture tests: gate.mjs must fail a page with only generic token names, pass a page with world-derived names, fail a fabricated testimonial, and PASS a page using PROC-03-style diegetic labels, which proves the claim guard does not fire on voice (C9); ledger.mjs must fail the round-8 recipe on an EMPTY ledger, pass two builds differing on ≥3 of 6 fingerprint fields, and veto the same build committed twice. Portability test: the full flow completes with sub-agents disabled and the only observable difference is the CRITIQUE: inline, not isolated banner. Product tests: A8 holdout — one unseen brief sealed before the build, baseline is upstream frontend-design plus a manual production pass (the strongest relevant arm, and the only one that beat SiteSmith), full site both sides, screenshots at three widths, blind adjudication, no new head-to-head arms; A9 — ledger.mjs --set across the holdout and two prototypes, requiring ≥3 of 6 fingerprint fields to differ for every pair. Honest-benchmark rule: if the holdout loses, the number is published as it landed, no re-run without a changed hypothesis.
candidates.weakestPoint: Deleting blocks/ is the riskiest deletion and I cannot prove it is right. A model authoring a mega-menu with a correct focus trap, or an accessible combobox, from memory will sometimes get it wrong. floor/app.md names the requirement and points at WAI-ARIA APG; nothing supplies an implementation. The failure is only partly detectable, because journeys are author-written — so a behaviour nobody thought to test is invisible to the gate that is supposed to catch it. gate.mjs fails a build with no journey for an interactive surface, which catches absence of testing, not absence of correctness. Close behind it: the anti-argmax step is self-graded prose. "Argue for the second thesis" can be rubber-stamped in one sentence and nobody would know. impeccable's hash-forced index, backed by its measured 30-of-35 identical concepts, is strictly stronger, and I traded it for A4 purity and one fewer script. The ledger veto is the backstop, but it fires at the end of a completed build, which is the most expensive possible place to discover the direction was typical.
candidates.whyItMightLose: The evidence supports "spend the instruction budget differently", and I have also spent it on deleting things the evidence never indicted. The measurement is about the ALWAYS-LOADED surface. Data corpora, block libraries and reference copies are not always-loaded — only 1.9% of the package loads on a routine run, so those 1.44 MB of CSVs cannot have caused the 40-vs-59 loss and deleting them cannot be credited with fixing it. A candidate that keeps them and only rewrites the always-loaded surface satisfies every number in INSTRUCTION-BUDGET-VS-QUALITY.md just as well, at lower risk. My extra deletions rest on a mechanism argument (corpora feed convergence, shared shapes produce shared shapes) that is plausible, forensically supported at n=1, and not measured — a reviewer is entitled to call them decorative. Second: a single always-loaded file is a single point of failure. If the re-expression smoke test comes back negative, a candidate with a routed creative layer can swap one route and re-test; MINIMAL has one surface, so a negative result invalidates the whole creative half at once. Third: coverage is visibly thinner and reviewers reward coverage — no blocks, no Vue/Svelte/Angular/Flutter/React Native adapters, one commerce file where v2.3 had a mode file plus a block library plus a products CSV. Against a candidate that keeps breadth, MINIMAL looks like a promise that a capable model will fill the gaps, and that promise is exactly what frontend-design made when it shipped a build judged not production-ready. Fourth: I dropped a confirmed, adopt-rated mechanism (structurally-different-direction-gate) on a reading of the round-8 evidence rather than on a measurement — it is equally defensible that the gate was too coarse and should have been made finer, and I picked the reading that supports my thesis. Fifth, and bluntly: 3,172 is not 2,078. The headline of this candidate is minimalism and the number is 1.53x the thing that won. If a rival lands closer to 2,078 while still satisfying A7 and A8, it beats MINIMAL at MINIMAL's own game.

candidates.routing: The model routes each SURFACE (not the project, not the company type) by what the visitor is doing: marketing / commerce / product-ui / experience. No script routes. Blends are named, both modules fetched, and the split recorded. No fifth route may be invented; an unroutable brief takes the closest route with a written mismatch note. The hard part is the decide/never-decide contract in SKILL.md §2: a route module MAY decide obligations, operable-vs-expressive surfaces, required journeys, gate profile, behaviour references and named failure modes; it may NEVER decide colour, ground, palette, typeface, type roles, radius, spacing step, shadow, texture, hero or section arrangement, motion character beyond the safety floor, copy voice, the signature element, or the one risk. Enforced three ways, not by prose: (1) fixed seven-heading schema — no eighth heading exists, so there is no place an appearance value can be written; (2) route-lint.mjs purity gate rejecting hex/rgb/hsl/oklch, font families, border-radius, box-shadow, font-size, letter-spacing, gradients, CSS lengths outside viewport widths/WCAG targets, and a banned-adjective list, with a tests/fixtures/impure-route.md control that must keep failing; (3) route-swap.mjs, which rebuilds one surface from the same DIRECTION.md under a deliberately wrong route and asserts BOTH invariance (computed tokens, fonts, radii, background layers and the signature element must not change — if the look changed when only the route changed, the router decided the design) and sensitivity (journeys, form/table semantics and obligations must change — a router that is safe by being inert should be deleted).
candidates.creativeLayer: The host model, reasoning from direction.md (1,502 est tokens, always loaded, route-independent), before any route module is fetched and before any script runs except stack detection. Method: pin subject/audience/page-job and commit; go into the subject's world (instruments, documents, units, what it prints and numbers, its vernacular, its fears) and name three photographable artifacts; name design tokens after things in that world rather than framework roles (--paper/--ink/--caution, not --bg/--surface/--accent) and write the token layer before components; type as identity; one cheap signature (three lines of CSS, no asset); one named risk against the category's own default; name the three current AI-design clusters as legitimate-when-asked-for but forbid ARRIVING there without a traceable reason; write five grounded directions and kill four with subject-specific reasons; run the counterfactual (work a neighbouring brief for a minute — if you land in the same place you found the category, change one structural thing and say what); copy as design material with voice free and claims gated. Convergence is stopped by seven layers, three of them measured: (1) generative rule indexed on the subject's world; (2) tokens named from the world so the first-written, most-steering layer cannot be shared; (3) five-direction shortlist with four killed (impeccable/forced-index-direction-roll, re-expressed without hash/catalogue/API); (4) counterfactual self-critique; (5) MEASURED — route-lint makes it structurally impossible for the routed layer to hold a shared appearance value; (6) MEASURED — diversity.mjs cross-build fingerprint veto plus portfolio-diversity gate, veto-only, never proposes; (7) MEASURED — route-swap invariance.

candidates.weakestPoint: The router's marginal value over a single conditional obligations file is unproven. If route modules contain no appearance and no taste, what they contain is production QA — and production QA does not obviously need routing. One obligations.md with conditional sections ('if money changes hands…', 'if the user is operating data…') would deliver the same duties and save the router table (~350 always-loaded tokens), the four-file split, the purity lint and the swap test. My defence is bulk — a checkout journey set has nothing in common with a dashboard's empty-state coverage, and separate files are what let each be complete without being always-loaded — but that is an argument about file size, not correctness, and a reviewer is entitled to call the router ceremony. Close behind: the purity lint catches syntax, not semantics ('the surface should feel spacious and considered' passes every check I specified and is a taste instruction; the banned-adjective list is a patch routed around by a synonym), route-swap is a release audit rather than a per-build guarantee because it requires building a surface twice, and the five-direction shortlist is prose-enforced with nothing distinguishing genuine generation from four directions reverse-engineered after the winner was already picked — a cost I accepted by dropping impeccable's hash, because a hash choosing the index would be a script deciding the design.
candidates.whyItMightLose: The one measurement that should drive this decision says the winner had one file, no router, no scripts, no data. This candidate reintroduces the exact structure that gallery/showcase.json records as producing 0/8 and defends it with a schema, a lint and a swap test — every one of which is new code that has never run. A flat candidate needs no defence because it has no attack surface; mine spends budget building a fence around a thing whose absence would be simpler and cheaper. Second, the arithmetic is against me on the only axis actually measured: 4,352 always-loaded tokens is 2.1x the entire skill that won 59-40. I argue most of that delta buys production capability frontend-design demonstrably lacked and that direction.md at 1,502 tokens is leaner on taste than the winner — but if the real mechanism behind 59-vs-40 was attention concentration rather than what the tokens said, then any candidate carrying a router table and a floor into always-loaded context is diluting the thing that won, and the flattest candidate wins on exactly the measured axis. Third, 'the router routes duties, not taste' is a distinction an adjudicator may reasonably refuse: required journeys imply mechanisms, mechanisms imply components, components imply layout. If a reviewer decides that cart persistence plus a sticky purchase control plus four required commerce journeys already determines most of what a shop page looks like, the purity claim is a relabelling and the house style returns through the obligations door. I think nordrig argues otherwise — build B had all those rules and still had a choosable look, it simply never chose one — but that is an interpretation of an n=1 comparison.

One overlay: existing code in the repo → read floors/redesign.md before touching anything. Extraction describes what is being replaced and lists what must survive; it never decides what to build. Clone/match/replicate is the one fidelity case and is never inferred.

What I deleted: v2.3's second routing axis (SETUP / NEW / REDESIGN / COMPONENT / AUDIT). A component request is a BUILD with one surface; an audit is a VERIFY with no BUILD; setup is a stack.mjs result. Collapsing them removes two orthogonal dimensions the model had to hold position in, and loses nothing measurable."
candidates.shape:
"Three layers plus a control plane, cut by who decides and at what moment — not by topic.

STANDARD (always loaded, ~1,400 est. tokens of SKILL.md §1–§6): prose, second person, aimed at judgement. Owns taste and the six-item universal floor.
FLOOR (fetched once at BUILD, one file, ~800–1,000 est. tokens): what this kind of surface must DO, stated as outcomes, never as appearance.
MACHINE (never in context as instruction, only as output): scripts, schema, one fact list. Zero always-loaded tokens.
CONTROL PLANE (always loaded, ~1,900 est. tokens of SKILL.md §7–§12): routing, four passes with stop conditions, state rule, precedence, scripts table. This is the literal price of A1 and A10.

The four passes are READ → THESIS → BUILD → VERIFY.

I rejected the topic split (creative / craft / production) because it puts the WHOLE craft floor always-loaded, which is backwards: v2.3's sixty always-open rules about what a page must contain are a description of a page, and three unrelated briefs got the same page. The correct cut runs INSIDE the floor — about eight items shape judgement continuously (155 tokens), the rest answer a question at a moment and are fetched then.

I rejected the capability split (build / redesign / audit / component) because it makes the creative surface a step rather than a standing condition, and a thesis you read once at step 4 is not in mind when you name the fourth colour at step 11."
candidates.weakestPoint: "vocabulary.mjs and the whole token-naming thesis rest on n=2 files. The single most load-bearing observation in this design is that nordrig build A's --paper/--grid/--caution steered its components while build B's --bg/--surface/--accent steered nothing, and NORDRIG-AB-FORENSICS.md says in its own words that this is one subject, one pair of builds, same host model writing both, and that a thesis step is NOT proven to cause the win in general. I turned that observation into a CI gate. It is also gameable: a model that renames --bg to --slate and declares slate a world noun defeats it completely, and I cannot detect that mechanically. The freeze-at-THESIS mitigation only stops post-hoc renaming, not a model that plans ahead."
candidates.whyItMightLose:
"1. It does not solve the core hypothesis, it only makes losing cheap. I do not know whether my re-expressed §1–§5 carries frontend-design's power. A candidate that instead ships frontend-design/SKILL.md VERBATIM — which Apache-2.0 permits — takes zero re-expression risk and could be judged strictly more evidence-led. My answer is a designed-in one-file swap, but 'we have a plan for when the hypothesis fails' is not evidence it will not.

2. pick.mjs is the most attackable thing here. A reader taking C-no-mechanical-creativity at its strongest says a hash function chose the design. My distinction — it chooses among the model's own designs and authors none — is real, but distinctions lose to slogans in adjudication. If it is struck, only the cross-build ledger and the naming discipline fight in-run convergence, which the 30/35 measurement says is the harder direction.

3. The always-loaded budget is 61% above the winner's: 3,352 vs 2,078. I argue the 1,900-token delta is control plane required by A1 and A10. But the one measurement this repo has is that more instruction did not buy better design, and nobody has measured 1,229 creative + 1,900 process against either arm. A leaner candidate that gets closer to 2,078 has the simpler story.

4. Deleting 57% of the package is irreversible in review terms. If an adjudicator values the accessibility tables or the font metadata, this candidate has no fallback and reads as reckless rather than disciplined.

5. Three floor files may converge at the floor layer. floor-lint constrains how floors are AUTHORED, not their effect. If every buy.md build lands on a sticky panel and a trust strip because that is where the floor spends its words, I have moved the house style down one layer and hidden it behind a lint — and the only detector is A9, which needs three builds to exist first.

6. No small-request bypass. 'Fix my pricing table' runs all four passes. That is absurd overhead and §8 does not address it."

See v2/40-interaction.md for what one contains.` — MINIMAL deletes all of v2/. The shipped script emits a dead pointer at exactly the moment the user needs guidance. On any fresh machine, any CI runner, or any second developer, the ledger is empty, so device 4 of the four anti-convergence devices reduces to the two hard-coded recipes. The primary mechanical guarantee against the exact failure the rebuild exists to fix is a home-directory file with no team, sync or CI story, and no stated fallback if the home directory is not writable.

THE CI REWRITE IS PRESENTED AS A REPOINT AND IS NOT. MINIMAL says 'tools/check-repo.py currently asserts REFS exists inside the skill; that assertion is repointed at docs/upstream/… a relocation of a structural check, not a relaxation'. In fact check-repo.py binds to the deleted material in at least five independent checks: _reference_line_counts (line 107-124) parses a routing table format with `| N |` line-count columns that MINIMAL's two-row table does not have; _datasets_reachable (line ~643) does `from core import CSV_CONFIG, STACK_CONFIG` — core.py is deleted; _doc_counts (line ~658) cross-checks 'N palettes / N CSV datasets' claims in README.md, NOTICE.md, SKILL.md and .claude-plugin/plugin.json against the deleted CSVs; the showcase gate excludes the generated blocks harness (line 715-717); plus the references TOC/group/hash checks at lines 214-574. TEST 0 IS THE GO/NO-GO AND CANNOT DETECT THE FAILURE IT MATTERS FOR. The re-expression smoke test is one brief, two builds, two reviewers, and MINIMAL says 'if our re-expression scores below the original, this candidate's premise is dead'. Round 8 is the standing evidence that single-site scoring does not detect the failure mode: gallery/showcase.json records individualReview pass and portfolioDiversity fail. MINIMAL states the principle itself — 'a single site cannot be measured for a property that only exists across a set' — and then stakes the whole creative half on a single-site comparison, n=1, unpowered, with 'no re-run without a changed hypothesis'.

TOKEN-DRIFT IS 'FOLDED IN' BUT ITS INPUT FORMAT IS DELETED. token-drift.mjs:241 requires a contract file containing a ```css block and points at references/12-design-system.md. MINIMAL replaces the contract with a five-line direction.md whose palette line is `--name #hex`. 'Folded into gate.mjs' understates a parser rewrite, and the same is true of production-gate.mjs's asset checks, which reference v2/24-asset-plan.md and v2/25-assets.md at five call sites (lines 223, 252, 388, 429, 440) that all become dead pointers.

'126 OF 139 FILES DELETED' CONFLATES MOVED WITH DELETED. Roughly 40 reference files plus THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json are relocated to docs/, not deleted, as the same document says three paragraphs earlier. Of the 13 shipped files, seven are retained v2.3 artifacts and six are new or rewritten. The headline compression figure is the most-quoted number in the candidate and it is not the number it describes.

C-no-unlicensed-text ENFORCEMENT NEEDS THE BANNED TEXT IN THE REPO. MINIMAL extends check-repo.py with 'a string scan for text traceable to website-builder-setup or redesign-skill'. A string scan needs a corpus to scan against; the two sources may not be copied at all. The candidate does not say where that corpus lives or how a paraphrase ban is checked without it.
overengineering: ledger.mjs's six-field render fingerprint is the single most expensive component in the design and it produces no better website. Four of six fields are bespoke visual detectors with no defined algorithm — 'device counts (uppercase-mono labels, hairline rules, tabular-figure blocks, flat-surface ratio)', 'signature share of viewport', 'macro-layout signature'. 'Signature share of viewport' requires mapping a free-text sentence from direction.md to a DOM subtree. Maintenance: every one of those detectors is a CSS-practice-dependent heuristic that drifts, it needs a browser, it writes global cross-machine state, and it fires only after a full build. Budgeted at ~14 KB replacing ~29 KB while adding three new fields — an unbuilt 2:1 compression claim on top of new capability.

The same free-text-to-DOM problem is reintroduced in gate.mjs check 4 ('the declared signature appears at all') — which is exactly the failure MINIMAL cites as the reason to shrink direction-fidelity.mjs: 'classifier regexes recognise only a fixed vocabulary of axis phrasing'. The candidate diagnoses the disease and then reimplements it twice, at a smaller size, and calls the smaller size the cure.

gate.mjs at ~18 KB is claimed to absorb production-gate.mjs (25.6 KB), token-drift.mjs (12.7 KB), direction-fidelity.mjs (23.2 KB) and a new antipattern lint and a new vocabulary check — a 4:1 compression while adding two capabilities and rewriting one parser. No basis is given. If it lands at 40 KB the maintenance argument for the merge disappears entirely.

gate.mjs check 4's 'the declared hexes account for the majority of rendered area' is a script asserting a compositional property. A photography-led or video-led hero, a full-bleed product image, or a map-heavy admin console legitimately fails it. No exemption is stated.

The five-line typed direction.md contract plus three mechanical fidelity assertions is a schema for an artifact whose value is that it is prose. Its enforced fields (four to six hexes, a display family, a signature) hard-code three universal design moves into the release gate for every build regardless of surface — including the internal admin console, where §8 itself says the visitor is only operating and convention should win.

A 30-line generic-token blocklist of 15-18 words masquerades as a convergence gate. It is trivially satisfied by a find-and-replace that renames --bg to --paper and changes nothing about the design, so its cost is a mandatory ritual and its yield is unmeasurable.
constraintViolations: C-no-mechanical-creativity / A4 — gate.mjs check 5 (world-derived token vocabulary) enforces a POSITIVE property of the token layer, and NORDRIG-AB-FORENSICS §1 is explicit that this is the layer that decides: 'the token layer is written before the components, so a subject-grounded token layer steers every component that follows'. MINIMAL's defence is 'it refuses a build that never made a decision', but the check cannot distinguish 'no decision' from 'a decision to use conventional names' (design-system deliverables, shadcn/Tailwind theming under C6, a redesign whose preserve-list pins existing tokens under C5). It is a new, unchallenged mechanism with no upstream source, no brief input, no override, and hard release authority over the layer the repo's own forensics calls decisive.

C-no-mechanical-creativity + the precedence ladder in §13 — ledger.mjs's hard-coded round-8 recipe and dark-ground ban fire on an EMPTY ledger, take no brief as input, and have no waiver. §13 rule 2 gives the client's explicit request precedence 'including a request that lands on a named default'. A script therefore overrides the brief. C7 blesses the veto SHAPE, so this is arguable rather than clear-cut, but C7 also says 'History may veto, never propose' — a recipe that fails on an empty ledger is not history, it is a ban list moved from prose into code, which is precisely what C1 resolved against ('naming beats banning… walls have a shape').

C-no-house-style — §4 bans a four-part recipe whose first element (uppercase mono labels) is taught eight lines later in §6 as the exemplar of good diegetic voice ('PROC-03', 'SLACK WATER'), in the same always-loaded file, with detection deferred to post-render. Separately, C1's own stated test is 'if all three avoid the same three clusters by using the same fourth thing, the rule has become a style' — MINIMAL mandates the same fourth thing on every build and enforces one part of it mechanically.

A10 (partial) — the candidate claims 'no loop whose exit depends on a subjective until it is good'. Two loops in SKILL.md are omitted from the five-loop table and have exactly that exit: §3's 'argue the case for the second as if the first did not exist' and §5's pass two, 'If you would arrive somewhere similar… change something structural and state what changed'. Both are revise-and-recheck loops with subjective, self-graded exit conditions and no integer cap. Also L4's grammar permits two consecutive 'rebuild' rounds, which by its own rule apply no fixes — a legal run that inspects twice and fixes nothing.
attacks.verdict:
Survives, but not as written — the creative thesis holds and the enforcement layer is where it is broken.

WHAT I COULD NOT KILL. The central argument is correct and the repo's own measurements back it: 2,078 tokens of standard-raising prose beat 6,546 tokens of output-describing prose, the cut-by-whether-output-is-a-design-decision test is the right test, verify.mjs is kept byte-for-byte so A7 stands, A1/A2 are clean (249 lines measured, no skill chain, §14 is attribution not instruction), C8 degrades honestly with a mandatory inline banner, no paid provider anywhere, and the licence position is defensible (nothing verbatim from website-builder-setup or redesign-skill; Apache/MIT obligations discharged by notices that stay in the bundle). Deleting the 86 KB Python direction engine really does make C-no-mechanical-creativity structural for the thing that scored 40. Its self-criticism is unusually honest — the weakestPoint and whyItMightLose sections named four of the problems before I did.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY BREAKS. Not in what it deleted from the creative surface. In what it built to replace the deleted enforcement. Every serious finding lands in the two NEW scripts and in the always-loaded file's internal contradictions:

1. The two new scripts reach into the design layer. gate.mjs check 5 mandates a naming vocabulary the repo's own forensics calls the decisive layer; ledger.mjs vetoes design regions on an empty ledger with no brief input. Both have hard release authority, neither has an override, and §12 forbids editing a check to pass. §13 says the brief wins; §12 says it cannot ship. That contradiction is in the always-loaded control plane, twelve lines apart.

2. It would converge, and I can trace it. Leather workshop, marine-cooling company, internal admin console all receive from §1-§6: world-noun custom properties (mechanically enforced), 4-6 colours, a display face distinct from body, exactly one signature with everything else quiet, one named risk against category default, and diegetic uppercase reference codes seeded by §6's own examples. HIDE-04, SW-INTAKE-02, TCK-118. Every one of those is a shared move, and the round-8 failure was five shared moves. The risk axis is worst: §5's only two exemplars are both ground-colour inversions ('a gaming shop on warm paper, a law firm that is not navy'), so the cheapest compliant risk on all three briefs is an unexpected ground colour. The admin console gets a signature element and an aesthetic risk it should not have, because §5 is unconditional while §8 correctly says operable surfaces follow convention.

3. Three verifiable factual errors. journey.mjs is kept byte-for-byte and points at a deleted file (journey.mjs:27 -> v2/40-interaction.md); its header does not contain 'the definition of a journey' as claimed. Deleting PIPELINE.json breaks bin/sitesmith.mjs:130 and with it the only automated playwright install, and the new SKILL.md has no install step, so A7 silently degrades to 'mechanical verdict missing' on every fresh machine. The gate that the candidate names as the mitigation for its own riskiest deletion is not in its own gate.mjs spec.

4. The budget headline is overstated. ROUTINE omits verify.md and stacks.md, both of which SKILL.md makes unconditional. Real floor 4,922 for any build, 6,422 for routine commerce (breaching its own proposed 6,000 gate), ~7,672 for a commerce redesign — above v2.3's always-loaded 6,546, which kills 'the worst case of the new skill is cheaper than the best case of the old one'. And the gate it proposes is vacuous against tools/context-budget.mjs as written, which hard-codes v2/ paths.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT SURVIVE PROPERLY. Four changes, none architectural: (a) add a brief-primacy waiver to gate.mjs check 5 and ledger.mjs, recorded in PRODUCTION-REPORT.md — otherwise a script outranks the client; (b) either drop check 5 or demote it to a warning until it has its own measurement, because it is new, unchallenged, trivially gamed by rename, and it manufactures a shared move across all builds; (c) reconcile §4 with §6 and add a second, non-colour exemplar to §5's risk line, or all three test briefs land on ground-colour inversion plus uppercase codes; (d) restore an install path and fix the journey.mjs pointer, or A7 is theatre on any machine that has not run the deleted installer.

ON THE MOST CONTESTABLE DROP. The candidate is right to be nervous about dropping structurally-different-direction-gate (adopt/confirmed in the ledger), but the drop is defensible on the record: round 8 shows all three comps passing the five-axis gate while the portfolio failed. The stronger criticism is not that it dropped the gate — it is that it replaced a coarse pre-render gate with a coarser POST-render one, moving detection from the cheapest point to the most expensive, and then admitted that in its own weakestPoint. That is a worse trade than the one it defends.

Verdict: no fatal flaw. The premise is the best-supported of anything in the rebuild docs. The execution ships two scripts that violate the constraint the candidate claims to have made structural, and an always-loaded file that teaches its own banned move.

attacks.verdict:
Buildable, and every hard constraint holds. What does not hold is the candidate's account of what building it costs.

VERIFIED FACTS. SKILL.md at 242 lines clears the 500-line cap (current is 196 lines / 11,160 B). verify.mjs is exactly 13,431 B and journey.mjs exactly 1,910 B as claimed. The four scripts gate.mjs replaces total 75,193 B ('~74 KB' — correct). The three ledger.mjs replaces total 28,622 B ('~29 KB' — correct). The Python engine totals 85,765 B ('86 KB' — correct). The NORDRIG section 1 token-vocabulary finding is real and is quoted accurately (A: --ink --paper --grid --steel --mute --caution --print --line; B: --bg --surface --surface-2 --border --text --muted --accent), and nothing in v2.3 checks it. C-no-mechanical-creativity becomes structural once design_system.py is gone. C-no-skill-chain, C-no-house-style, A10 and A2 all hold.

CONTROL GROUP: STILL FAILS. I served benchmarks/ and ran the unmodified verify.mjs against benchmarks/06-redesign/before/ — FAIL, 13 blocking issues (color-contrast at 2.29 and 2.53 in both light and dark, eight placeholder href="#" links). Since verify.mjs is kept byte-for-byte and the fixture is untouched, A7 and C-control-group survive intact. This is the one part of the plan that needs no work at all.

WHAT SURVIVES / IS REWRITTEN / IS DELETED, concretely. Survives untouched: SKILL.md's slot (rewritten content), scripts/verify.mjs, scripts/journey.mjs (one line must change — see problems), scripts/package.json, LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt (LICENSES/MIT.txt does not exist today and must be created), THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (needs an honesty decision). Rewritten: SKILL.md, THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json, and two new scripts absorbing seven old ones. Deleted: all 10 references/*.md, all 35 references/impeccable/*.md, all 28 data/*.csv, all 22 blocks/ files, all 18 v2/ files, 16 of 20 scripts (asset-plan, candidates.py, core.py, critique-gate, design_system.py, direction-check, direction-fidelity, direction-history, direction-record, portfolio-diversity, production-gate, search.py, stack-router, token-drift, visual-assets, plus __pycache__), and PIPELINE.json — which the file tree omits without saying so, and which bin/sitesmith.mjs:130 needs to generate every provider pack.

REALISTIC BUILD ORDER — and the order the candidate implies is the wrong one. The proposal is framed as 'delete 126 of 139 files', which invites deletion first. Do not. Deleting data/ alone makes `python tools/check-repo.py` unimportable at line 646 (`from core import CSV_CONFIG`), so the repo loses its own self-check before a replacement exists, and one commit turns at least eleven CI steps red simultaneously with no green baseline to bisect. Correct order: (1) write SKILL.md sections 1-7 and run Test 0, the re-expression smoke test, before anything else is built — the candidate is right that this is the cheapest possible falsification and it needs no deletions; (2) write gate.mjs and ledger.mjs alongside the existing scripts, with their eight fixtures, while CI is still green; (3) rewrite tools/check-repo.py and regenerate THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json for the new layout, including the schema change needed to reference docs/upstream/; (4) rewire verify.yml — replace test-product-flow, test-direction-format, test-direction-history, gate-fixtures, showcase-gate, the block-harness steps and the clean-install PIPELINE.json assertion; (5) rewrite tools/context-budget.mjs so ROUTINE means something, then set the gate; (6) delete, in one commit, with CI already expecting the new shape; (7) A8 holdout and A9.

FIRST THING TO GO WRONG. Whoever starts with the deletion. Second most likely: the implementer reads 'check-repo.py enforces SKILL.md under 500 lines, hash-matched licence texts and notices' from the test plan, opens the file expecting a short script, and finds a 330-line provenance checker pinned to 75 files, six groups with exact counts, per-file and per-span SHA-256s, a reconstructed-source tree hash for impeccable, and a hard-coded 32-link reconstruction. That check alone is a day.

HOURS: 80–130 for a competent implementer with this repo open. Roughly 25-35 h for the prose (SKILL.md plus five fetched files), 25-40 h for gate.mjs, ledger.mjs and their fixtures, and 30-45 h for check-repo.py, the provenance manifest, context-budget.mjs and the verify.yml rewiring — that last third being the part the candidate does not mention at all. Test 0, the A8 holdout and A9 add 15-25 h on top if they are counted as build work rather than evaluation.

BOTTOM LINE. The architecture is sound and nothing here is unbuildable. The candidate is honest about its creative risks and dishonest by omission about its engineering ones: it presents itself as the low-cost option and its true cost is dominated by CI and provenance plumbing that is nowhere in the plan. If it is selected, the plan needs a fourth layer added to its own three-layer test — 'what in the repository executes against the files I am deleting' — and the answer is eleven CI steps, five fixture trees and the installer.

fatalFlaws.claim: route-swap.mjs cannot pass: its invariance and sensitivity assertions are mutually exclusive, and it has no same-route control arm for generation nondeterminism. Because a route-swap failure is a non-retryable release blocker, the holdout (A8) has no path to a release verdict.
fatalFlaws.why: The test rebuilds one surface under a deliberately wrong route from the same DIRECTION.md and requires BOTH that 'the set of computed colour values, font families, radius values and background layers, plus the presence of the declared signature element' match, AND that 'the journey set, the form/table semantics and the declared obligations must differ'. Sensitivity is what guarantees invariance fails. Build a product page under commerce, then under product-ui: commerce demands a purchase control, price figures, trust elements and unavailable-option states; product-ui demands empty/loading/error/permission-denied states, a sortable table, bulk select and destructive-action confirmation. Different components mean a different set of computed colour values in use (an accent on a purchase control versus a destructive-action colour and disabled states), different radius values (a sticky panel has one, a table row does not) and different background layers (a sticky panel introduces a surface layer). Either the tolerance is tight and the test always fails, or it is loose enough that it only asserts 'all values came from DESIGN-SYSTEM.md' — which is contract.mjs, already in the script list, and needs no second build. Separately, both arms are LLM-generated, so there is no null condition: a diff between two generations under different routes cannot be attributed to the route without a same-route rebuild to measure baseline variance, and the candidate specifies no such control. Consequence for A8: §8 says route-swap failure 'is a release blocker, not a retry trigger' and §12 test 7 requires both verdicts on the holdout. A test that cannot pass and cannot be retried means the holdout build can never reach a release verdict. And because route-swap is the only mechanism converting 'the router does not decide the look' from an assertion into a measurement, its collapse reduces the candidate to v2.3 routing with the appearance headings deleted, defended by a syntax lint.

attacks.verdict: Killed on two counts, neither of which is the router. Count one: the candidate's always-loaded direction.md prescribes, as its preferred signature, exactly the devices that skills/sitesmith/scripts/direction-history.mjs hard-codes as the round-8 known-bad recipe — ruled ground and margin rule are hairline separators, a numbering system and 'the numbering the trade actually uses' are mono-uppercase labels and tabular figures, 'three lines of CSS and no asset' is flat surfaces — and routes/commerce.md obligation 1 ('a figure that lines up between rows') plus routes/product-ui.md's table obligations mandate the fourth device through the obligations door while passing route-lint cleanly. The skill therefore instructs the recipe, mandates part of it, vetoes the combination in a script, and then ships it after one re-entry 'with the collision named'. A9 is unreachable as written. Trace it on the three briefs: a leather workshop, a marine-cooling company and an internal admin console all get a trade document as their world (the only worked example in the file is a drawing office, `--paper --ink --caution --grid --steel`), all three get a hairline-ruled ground with mono reference codes and tabular units, none gets elevation or raster imagery — and the 'one risk against your own category' rule makes it worse, not better, because systematically inverting each category's default rotates all three into one another's palette family, which is verbatim what docs/v2/preflight/round-8/diversity/portfolio.json already recorded: 'one palette recipe with the hue rotated'. Count two: route-swap.mjs, the mechanism that supposedly turns the candidate's whole thesis from a promise into a measurement, cannot pass. Its sensitivity assertion (obligations, journeys and form/table semantics must differ) guarantees the component sets differ, which guarantees the invariance assertion (same computed colour values, radii and background layers) fails; loosen the tolerance until it passes and the test reduces to contract.mjs, which is already in the script list and needs no second build. There is also no same-route control arm, so a diff between two LLM generations cannot be attributed to the route at all. Because §8 makes route-swap failure a non-retryable release blocker and §12 requires both verdicts on the holdout, A8 has no path to a release verdict either. Both are repairable — delete the signature-preference menu and the 'numbering/units' steer, and demote route-swap to a non-blocking diagnostic with a same-route baseline — so the adjudicator should not read this as a verdict against routing per se. The honest state of the router argument after this review is worse than the candidate's own §13 admits: the purity gate covers routes/*.md only, leaving the script-selected adapters, ten behaviour references and four corpora unaudited; the load-bearing mechanism sitesmith-current/mode-based-routing-not-defaults is redTeam 'unchallenged' at confidence 0.7 and inherited from the 0/8 build, while the candidate drops taste-skill/full-output-enforcement explicitly for being unchallenged; and the candidate's own bulk defence for four route files collapses on its own numbers, since the entire routes/ directory is roughly 3,500 estimated tokens against a 4,352-token always-loaded budget. Five subdirectories under references/ for ten files (commerce/2, product-ui/2, experience/2, marketing/1, common/3). marketing/proof.md is a single file in its own directory.

attacks.verdict:
Buildable, and better grounded in this repository than its own summary suggests — but its differentiator does not work as specified, and its testing section understates the CI bill by roughly an order of magnitude.

WHAT SURVIVES / IS REWRITTEN / IS DELETED, concretely:
Survives untouched: verify.mjs (I ran it against benchmarks/06-redesign/before/ — exit 1, 13 blocking issues, so C-control-group holds), LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt (sha-pinned), THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md (7 phrase assertions still satisfied), gallery/showcase.json + index.html (status reset, passes unchanged), the root LICENSE.
Renamed with real surgery: stack-router.mjs→stack.mjs (adapter target changes CSV→md, plus a new `plain` path that removes its refuse-to-guess property), token-drift.mjs→contract.mjs (thinnest change of the set), journey.mjs→journeys.mjs (needs a required-journey manifest that does not exist), portfolio-diversity.mjs + direction-history.mjs→diversity.mjs (~25 KB merge).
Rewritten from scratch: search.py→fetch.py (search.py is a CLI over core.py + design_system.py, both deleted), production-gate.mjs→tells.mjs (25.5 KB carve-out, and the candidate keeps the unmanifested-image check while deleting the manifest it reads).
Deleted: v2/ (18 files), blocks/ (21+ files), data/ (30 files), references/ (46 files incl. 35 impeccable), PIPELINE.json, THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json, core.py, design_system.py, candidates.py, direction-check.mjs, direction-fidelity.mjs, direction-history.mjs, direction-record.mjs, critique-gate.mjs, asset-plan.mjs, visual-assets.mjs.
check-repo.py under the proposal: 6 of 16 checks hard-fail (_runtime_task_routes, _third_party_provenance, _datasets_reachable, _doc_counts, _search_smoke, _design_system_smoke — the last four crash on `from core import …` or a missing data/colors.csv), 4 more pass vacuously (_reference_line_counts, _attribution, _change_notices, _toc, all of which glob references/*.md and find nothing), 6 genuinely pass. Baseline note: check-repo.py is red TODAY with 14 dead-link failures, all from docs/rebuild/candidates/layered.md and minimal.md. routed.md contributes zero — it wrote its file tree without markdown links. That is the only candidate currently not breaking the gate it will have to satisfy.

REALISTIC BUILD ORDER: (1) branch, freeze v2/ rather than deleting, write direction.md + floor.md + SKILL.md; (2) run the pre-registered re-expression A/B immediately — it is the cheapest kill and everything downstream assumes it passes; (3) write route-lint.mjs and both fixtures, then write the four route modules against the lint; (4) rewire the seven scripts; (5) write the missing provenance generator and rebuild the manifest; (6) rewrite check-repo.py's six broken checks, gate-fixtures.mjs, test-product-flow.mjs, and strip the blocks/PIPELINE steps from verify.yml; (7) two prototypes → route-swap audit → diversity → holdout.

FIRST THING THAT GOES WRONG: step 3, not step 6. Writing commerce.md's obligations without appearance. v2/modes/ecommerce.md's real content is 'the purchase path owns the accent colour', 'prices in tabular mono', 'sticky buy panel', 'trust strip' — every one is appearance or one step from it. `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` passes every pattern the candidate lists (it is not a hex, a font-family, a radius, a shadow or a length), yet portfolio-diversity.mjs counts tabular figures as one of the five shared devices that produced the round-8 house style, and direction-history.mjs's KNOWN_RECIPES exists to trip on exactly that combination. So the first route module either fails its own lint or passes it while carrying the device the whole candidate was built to prevent. That collision is the weakestPoint made operational, and it lands on day two.

ESTIMATE: 110-170 hours for a competent implementer with this repo open. Breakdown: creative surface + A/B 8-14; four routes + schema + lint + fixtures 14-22; ten references + four adapters + four corpora 16-26; seven rewired scripts 18-28; route-swap (with the null arm it currently lacks) 10-16; provenance generator + check-repo.py rewrite 16-26; CI and tools repair 12-20; prototypes, holdout, no-sub-agent run, fake-edge and blend tests 14-24. fatalFlaws.claim: pick.mjs is a script that decides the design. It violates C-no-mechanical-creativity literally and fails A4 as written — and it is unauditable and trivially bypassable, so it buys nothing in exchange.
fatalFlaws.why: C-no-mechanical-creativity enumerates the permitted verbs: "Scripts verify, retrieve and gate." Selecting is a fourth verb. A4 says "No script output is allowed to be the design decision." SKILL.md §2 makes the output binding — "It returns an index that is never 0 … Build that one" — with one override per build. On any build where the override is spent, a sha256 of (subject + date) is the final authority on which thesis is built, and the thesis determines the token vocabulary, the signature, the typographic identity and the risk. That is the design. Worse, the mechanism cannot be audited or enforced: the candidate list is never persisted. The §9 schema stores only thesis.candidates_written (a count) and thesis.picked_index. Nothing records what the seven candidates were or in what order they were written, so no script, no CI check and no reviewer can tell whether the model wrote its list before or after running pick.mjs. Since pick.mjs takes only --subject and --count, a model can run it first, read the index, and then author its list so its favourite sits at that index. The mechanism is defeated by reordering two steps, and the state file is designed so that this is undetectable. The candidate's own §15.2 concedes it may lose in adjudication but keeps it anyway; the deeper problem is that it is a hard-constraint violation that purchases an unverifiable benefit.
fatalFlaws.evidence: docs/rebuild/CHARTER.md:51 (C-no-mechanical-creativity) and :39 (A4). docs/rebuild/candidates/layered.md §2 of the embedded SKILL.md (lines 227–245): "Then run node scripts/pick.mjs --subject … --count … It returns an index that is never 0 … Build that one." §9 schema (lines 645–651) stores candidates_written and picked_index but no candidate list. §15.2 (lines 896–901) admits the exposure.

fatalFlaws.claim: The anti-house-style veto (7.2, history.mjs) is invoked at THESIS, where four of its six fingerprint dimensions — and all four devices of the hard-coded round-8 known-bad recipe — are uncomputable. The CI regression it relies on tests a fixture, not the product. A9 is therefore unenforced by the only mechanism assigned to it.
fatalFlaws.why: §8 THESIS: "Then node scripts/history.mjs check against your own past builds. A match is a veto and you move." §7.2 defines the fingerprint as covering "palette buckets, display/body type class, surface treatment, label treatment, figure treatment, depth treatment" of the RENDERED page. At THESIS the state file contains only tokens (hex), type_roles, a prose signature and a prose risk. The candidate deleted v2.3's four machine-readable grammar fields (surface, labels, figures, depth) when it dropped sitesmith-current/structurally-different-direction-gate, and its §9 schema has no replacement field for any of them. Reading the actual implementation settles it: devicesFromFingerprint() derives mono-uppercase-labels from a count monoCaps>=4, hairline-separators from hairlines>=20, tabular-figure-motif from tabularNums>=3 and flat-surfaces from shadowed===0. Those are DOM element counts. The candidate has no comps (direction-check.mjs and direction-record.mjs are on the delete list) and no render at THESIS, so there is nothing to count. The round-8 recipe — the repo's one measured house style, the failure the whole rebuild exists to fix — is defined entirely in terms the candidate made uncomputable at the moment it checks for it. The CI requirement that it "must keep tripping on a clean install" will pass forever against a synthetic fingerprint object while never firing in a real build. That is a claimed benefit with no way to verify. The alternative reading — that the veto really fires at VERIFY — is worse: §10 caps re-rolls at 2, so a veto after the build means up to three full site builds per job, a cost nowhere in the budget.
fatalFlaws.evidence: docs/rebuild/candidates/layered.md, embedded SKILL.md §8 THESIS (lines 348–355) and §7.2 (lines 516–527); §9 schema (lines 635–665) — no surface/labels/figures/depth field; §12 delete table (line 787) drops structurally-different-direction-gate; file tree (lines 138–140) deletes direction-check.mjs and direction-record.mjs. Implementation: skills/sitesmith/scripts/direction-history.mjs:29–37 (KNOWN_RECIPES devices) and :51–63 (devicesFromFingerprint reads monoCaps, hairlines, tabularNums, shadowed, cards — all render counts); the v2.3 CLI signature is `direction-history.mjs check DIRECTION.md <winner-url>` (skills/sitesmith/SKILL.md:73), i.e. it required a rendered URL.

fatalFlaws.claim: The always-loaded file teaches the exact house style it forbids. §1, §4 and §5 hold up nordrig build A as the exemplar; §3 cluster 3 and history.mjs's KNOWN_RECIPES name nordrig A's own devices as SiteSmith's forbidden house style. A model that follows the creative sections well produces the artifact the ledger is hard-coded to veto.
fatalFlaws.why: §1's canonical good example is nordrig A's token layer (--paper --grid --caution --steel). §4's only worked signature example is A's blueprint grid ("three lines of CSS"). §5's only worked copy example is A's PROC-03 — an uppercase mono reference label. Per NORDRIG-AB-FORENSICS, A also uses mono part labels, 01 02 03 step numbering, a spec-block definition list on hairline rules, and a flat light paper ground with no depth. Now read §3 cluster 3, which the candidate itself labels SiteSmith's own past output and says is drifting toward a house style: "broadsheet layout, hairline rules, uppercase mono labels, tabular figures as a motif". And KNOWN_RECIPES.technical-editorial-flat = mono-uppercase-labels + hairline-separators + tabular-figure-motif + flat-surfaces. The exemplar and the anti-pattern are the same artifact on at least three of four devices, and the prose gives the model no way to distinguish them — §3 says the tell is "arriving there without choosing", which is a statement about the model's internal process, not about anything on the page or in the fingerprint. So the file simultaneously instructs the round-8 recipe and vetoes it. Concretely: a well-executed build burns both re-rolls and then, by §10, ships "the least-colliding candidate rather than looping" — i.e. the architecture's stated outcome for its best work is to build the worse idea. This is not a wording slip; it is the load-bearing exemplar of the creative layer colliding with the load-bearing seed of the anti-convergence layer, and it makes A9 unreachable through the intended path.

seriousProblems: ROUTINE budget is wrong for the most common commercial build, and breaches the candidate's own CI ceiling. §7 mandates routing PER SURFACE ("A shop's About page is decide; its order console is operate"), but §4's budget table and the file tree both assume exactly one floor file is loaded. A normal e-commerce site loads decide.md + buy.md + operate.md. Using the candidate's own numbers: 3,352 + 3x1,000 + 750 (stack) = 7,102, against the A3 gate it sets itself at ROUTINE 6,500. With floors/redesign.md as well it is ~7,900. The claimed 5,102 only holds for a single-surface site.

state-fields-consumed.mjs, the novel lint that section 9 offers as the proof that typed state is not ceremony, does not work as specified. It "greps the scripts for each field name" — but the scripts take CLI arguments, not state fields. pick.mjs receives --subject and --count (§14, A4 row: "pick.mjs takes a subject string and a count and nothing else"), so the schema's `subject: consumedBy pick.mjs, history.mjs`, `candidates_written: consumedBy pick.mjs` and `picked_index: consumedBy pick.mjs` are all false; pick.mjs never reads state.json. `fingerprint` is annotated consumedBy history.mjs but the same line says "(written at VERIFY)" — written, not read. Either the lint is strict and deletes four fields the design needs, or it is a loose substring grep that passes everything and proves nothing. Section 9's claim that it makes "is this ceremony?" a test rather than an argument does not survive contact with its own schema.

vocabulary.mjs punishes correct design on operate surfaces, contradicting §7. Its generic blocklist is bg, surface, accent, primary, secondary, muted, border, card, foreground, ring, input, popover, destructive. §7 says convention is kept where the visitor is operating — tables, forms, errors, nav. On a dashboard, --border, --muted and --card are the semantically correct names, and the gate fails the build for using them. Nothing exempts operate surfaces from the vocabulary floor. For an internal admin console with no trade world, §1 forces the model to invent one anyway ("name it yourself"), so the mechanism converts a console into a themed marketing site to satisfy a linter. The pass threshold is also never stated anywhere in the candidate — an unspecified floor on a gate is an unfalsifiable gate plus a tuning knob.

antipattern.mjs is an appearance ban list that is exempt from every anti-house-style control the candidate built. floor-lint.mjs bans hex values, font names, radii and spacing scales in floors/*.md; it says nothing about scripts. Per the ledger, impeccable/mechanical-antipattern-detector is a 59-rule registry of named AI-tell patterns mapped to static HTML/CSS checks — i.e. exactly a list of appearance rules, applied identically to every build, invisible to floor-lint and to portfolio-diversity (which measures outcomes, not causes). The ledger's own recorded failure mode is "frozen snapshot of one aesthetic era". The appearance rules the candidate expels from prose simply relocate into code.

floor-lint.mjs constrains the wrong vocabulary. It bans appearance VALUES but not structural prescriptions. buy.md is specified to carry "exactly nordrig build B's list" — purchase path, sticky buy panel, mobile bottom bar, trust strip, tabular figures, no motion near money. None of those is a hex, a font name, a radius or a spacing scale, so all of them pass the lint and appear in every commerce build. The "Three ways" requirement is also satisfiable by paraphrase: "a warm ground" is lint-clean and means #f4f1e8. The candidate's own §15.4 concedes the effect is unconstrained; the sharper point is that the lint is scoped to a vocabulary that was never the convergence risk.

Licence problem in the designed-in contingency. The embedded SKILL.md frontmatter declares `license: MIT` (line 194). §14 pre-commits: "If arm B loses by more than 4 points, §1–§5 are replaced by a verbatim include of frontend-design/SKILL.md, which Apache-2.0 permits with notice." Apache-2.0 text cannot be relicensed as MIT; a verbatim include obliges retaining the Apache-2.0 licence and NOTICE for that portion, and the file as designed would then misstate its own licence. C-licence and A5 both bite. Fixable with a per-section licence note, but it is not noted anywhere.

The decision rule for the smoke test that the candidate says decides whether it is right at all is statistically meaningless. S10-1 is n=1 (one brief, two builds), scored by the same blind protocol that produced 59 vs 40, and the trigger is a 4-point margin. A 5-point loss forces a rewrite of the creative layer; a 3-point loss ships it. Nothing establishes that the rubric resolves 4 points, and CHARTER.md budget policy sets "Re-runs without a changed hypothesis: 0", so the noise can never be reduced. The contingency is well-designed as an architecture (one file swap) and undefined as a criterion.

No small-request path, and this is the part of the design most likely to be silently discarded. "Fix my pricing table" runs READ (up to 3 lettered questions), THESIS (5–7 candidate theses, pick.mjs, history veto), BUILD and VERIFY (six scripts). §2 argues COMPONENT and AUDIT collapse into BUILD-with-one-surface and VERIFY-with-no-BUILD, but §8 never wires that in — the four passes are stated as a mandatory sequence with THESIS in the middle, so an audit of an existing site still has to invent a thesis and roll a pick index. In practice the model will skip passes, which makes the control plane advisory — and the control plane is the entire justification for the 1,900-token overage over frontend-design.

Two loops have no checkable stop condition, against A10. §10 records "small deviations unbounded and noted" and "Preview render while editing: none [no cap]". The deviation policy's real stop — "a contradiction that changes the thesis, stop and say so" — requires the model to classify its own deviation as small versus thesis-level, with no artifact, no script and no threshold. That is the row the candidate itself says is "usually faked", relocated one step earlier.

Portfolio diversity (A9's checker) has no data source in repo CI. history.jsonl lives in ~/.sitesmith/ on the operator's machine and "stores no client URLs"; tools/portfolio-diversity.mjs runs "across the last N recorded builds" in repo CI. Nothing states where those recorded builds come from, or that the tool fails closed on an empty or short ledger. As specified, A9's gate passes trivially until three builds happen to exist on whichever machine runs CI. The ledger's own recorded failure mode for the anti-repeat ledger is "local to one machine, doesn't travel with repo/team".

Nine adopted mechanisms are red-team `unchallenged` and are treated as confirmed: frontend-design/signature-element-restraint, frontend-design/copy-as-design-material, taste-skill/full-output-enforcement, before-implementing/deviation-policy, before-implementing/self-contained-packaging-lesson, sitesmith-current/portfolio-diversity-gate, sitesmith-current/verify-fail-closed-gates, sitesmith-current/mode-based-routing-not-defaults. MECHANISM-LEDGER.md states plainly that "unchallenged means the red team did not examine it, which is weaker than confirmed, and is kept as a separate state on purpose". Section 12 flattens that distinction without saying so. Notably, copy-as-design-material and signature-element-restraint are two of the five pillars of the creative layer, and portfolio-diversity-gate is A9's checker.

The three-mode routing is coarser than the mechanism it cites. impeccable/mode-based-visitor-registers has four registers (Persuade / Operate / Read / Experience) and the ledger already flags "coarse taxonomy; blended-mode surfaces aren't well covered; no check catches a wrong classification". The candidate drops to three by folding Read and Experience into decide.md, so a landing page, an editorial magazine, a documentation site, a portfolio and every About page in the world load one identical file that prescribes "what the hero must resolve" and "conversion paths". That is a convergence vector introduced by the routing, on top of the ones already conceded in §15.4.
overengineering: state-fields-consumed.mjs plus the consumedBy annotation on every schema property. It does not work as specified (scripts read CLI flags), and every rename of a state field or a script argument breaks CI. It produces no better website; it is a lint whose entire purpose is to prove that a different piece of ceremony is not ceremony.

pick.mjs and its supporting apparatus: a hash function, two schema fields, an override-rate CI check across builds, and a protocol whose correctness cannot be observed because the candidate list is never persisted. Cost: one script, three CI surfaces, an argument to defend in adjudication. Benefit: unmeasurable by construction.

floor-lint.mjs's "## Three ways" requirement. It mechanises prose authoring — a CI check that counts list items in markdown — and forces the maintainer to write three renditions of every non-obvious outcome across four floor files, forever, on pain of a red build. It is satisfiable by paraphrase and it does not touch the structural prescriptions that actually converge.

data/font-families.txt, ~1,800 Google Font names with no metadata. No script in the tree consumes it and no rule in SKILL.md references it. If the model reads it to choose a typeface, it is a seeded menu shaping the design — the very thing that got ui-ux-pro-max/static-ux-knowledge-tables and data/typography.csv deleted, only worse, because a bare name list carries no reasoning at all. If the model never reads it, it is ~20 KB of dead weight. Either way it fails the candidate's own consumption rule.

schema/state.schema.json as a typed contract. Of the ~15 fields drafted in §9, five have a real machine consumer (surfaces, thesis.world_nouns, tokens, claims, fingerprint). Two are deleted by the lint in the draft itself (audience, job). Three (thesis.sentence, signature, risk) survive only by nominating the model's own later critique as their "consumer", which is not a script and defeats the rule.

Four separate shipped-artifact parsers — token-drift.mjs, vocabulary.mjs, antipattern.mjs and production-gate.mjs — each independently reading the built HTML/CSS. Four parsers, four sets of selector assumptions, four things that break when a stack changes how it emits CSS.

Eight new or rewritten scripts required before the first build: pick.mjs, vocabulary.mjs, antipattern.mjs, state.mjs, stack.mjs (rename/rewrite of stack-router.mjs), history.mjs (rewrite of direction-history.mjs), plus repo tools floor-lint.mjs and state-fields-consumed.mjs. The candidate presents the Machine layer as "kept from v2.3, works"; only verify.mjs, journey.mjs, token-drift.mjs and production-gate.mjs actually exist today.
constraintViolations: C-no-mechanical-creativity (CHARTER.md:51) — violated. pick.mjs neither verifies, retrieves nor gates; it selects, and SKILL.md §2 makes the selection binding ("Build that one"), with one override per build. After the override is spent, a hash is the final authority on the design direction.

A4 (CHARTER.md:39, "No script output is allowed to be the design decision") — violated by the same mechanism. The candidate's proposed check for A4 ("pick.mjs receives a subject string and a count and nothing else") tests the script's inputs, not whether its output decides the design, which is what the criterion says.

C-licence / A5 — violated by the designed-in contingency. §14 pre-commits to a verbatim include of Apache-2.0 frontend-design/SKILL.md into a file whose frontmatter declares `license: MIT` (embedded SKILL.md line 194). Apache-2.0 text cannot be relicensed MIT; notice and licence retention are required for the included portion.

(a) §3 does not merely name clusters 3 and 4; it says "if your page is drifting toward them, it is drifting toward a house style", which is a ban, and C1's own recorded failure mode is that the ban list becomes the shape. (b) antipattern.mjs is a fixed appearance ban list applied to every build, exempt from floor-lint.mjs and invisible to portfolio-diversity.mjs.

attacks.verdict:
Does not survive as submitted. Three flaws are fatal, and all three are provable from the candidate's own documents plus the code in this repo.

1. pick.mjs violates C-no-mechanical-creativity and A4 literally — a script's output is the binding design decision — and it is simultaneously unauditable and bypassable, because the state file stores only a count and an index, never the candidate list. Nothing can tell whether the model wrote its seven candidates before or after reading the index. It is a hard-constraint violation that purchases an unverifiable benefit. Strike it and §7.1 disappears, leaving nothing aimed at the in-run 30/35 convergence the candidate itself calls the harder direction.

2. The anti-house-style veto cannot fire. §8 invokes history.mjs check at THESIS; §7.2 defines the fingerprint over rendered-page properties; direction-history.mjs derives every device in the hard-coded round-8 recipe from DOM counts (monoCaps>=4, hairlines>=20, tabularNums>=3, shadowed===0). The candidate deleted v2.3's declared surface/labels/figures/depth grammar fields and its rendered comps, and added no replacement to the §9 schema. So the one mechanism pointed at the repo's one measured house style checks for it at the only moment it is uncomputable. The CI requirement that the recipe "must keep tripping on a clean install" will pass forever against a synthetic fixture while never firing in a real build. That is a claimed benefit with no way to verify.

3. The always-loaded surface teaches the style it forbids. §1's exemplar token layer, §4's exemplar signature and §5's exemplar copy are all nordrig build A — world-noun tokens, a CSS texture, PROC-03 mono labels, spec-block hairline rules, a flat light ground. §3 cluster 3 and KNOWN_RECIPES.technical-editorial-flat name that same set of devices as SiteSmith's forbidden house style. A model that follows the creative sections well produces the artifact the ledger is seeded to veto, burns both re-rolls, and then by §10 ships "the least-colliding candidate" — the worse idea, by design.

Traced concretely across a leather workshop, a marine-cooling company and an internal admin console, the architecture pushes all three toward the same move set: 4–6 trade-noun CSS variables (mandated by §1, gated by vocabulary.mjs against a fixed generic blocklist), a cheap CSS-generated background texture as the signature (§4's only worked example), diegetic reference labels and eyebrows (§5's only worked example), and one deliberate risk. That is nordrig A generalised — a house style, arrived at through the creative layer rather than the craft floor. The admin console is the clearest failure: it has no trade world, §1 forces it to invent one, and vocabulary.mjs penalises the semantically correct names (--border, --muted, --card) that §7 says convention should keep on operating surfaces.

What is genuinely good and should survive into whatever wins: the who-decides-and-when layering is the right axis, and the argument for cutting inside the craft floor rather than around it is correct and better reasoned than the topic split in the S2 forensics. The always-loaded arithmetic is honest — I recounted the embedded SKILL.md at 249 lines and 13,408 bytes against a claimed 13,409, and the §1–§5 and §7–§12 subtotals add up. No adopted mechanism is marked refuted, and the claim that all 12 `investigate` entries are refutation-derived is exactly right. The designed-in one-file swap for the re-expression risk is the best structural answer to the core hypothesis that any candidate has offered.

Two claims in the write-up are not honest, and both are checkable arithmetic. First, "Package total falls from ~630k est. tokens to roughly 45k" silently excludes references/ (121,839 est. tokens) while the file tree explicitly retains references/ and the 630k baseline it is compared against includes it. Recomputed from BASELINE-CONTEXT-BUDGET.json with the stated deletions and references/ kept: ~172k est. tokens, off by 3.8x. Without references/ it is ~50k, close to the claim — so the two figures are measured with different rulers, and the "delete 57%" argument rests on the mismatch. Second, ROUTINE ≈ 5,100 assumes one floor file while §7 mandates per-surface routing; an ordinary shop loads three floors and lands at ~7,100 against the candidate's own 6,500 CI ceiling.

Minimum to make this reviewable again: delete §2 and pick.mjs, or replace the binding language with the model choosing a non-top candidate itself and recording which and why; restore four declared grammar fields to the state schema so the THESIS veto has something to read, or move the veto to VERIFY and cost the rebuild; and resolve the §3-versus-§5 exemplar collision by naming what distinguishes A's diegetic labels from the round-8 recipe in terms visible on the page rather than in the model's intentions. The first two are deletions and a schema edit. The third is the hard one, and it is the actual open problem the rebuild has not solved.

fatalFlaws.claim: The deletion list breaks the third-party provenance contract, which is hash-pinned in two independent CI validators and has no generator in the repo. The candidate's file tree also omits THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json entirely.
fatalFlaws.why: skills/sitesmith/THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json (41,871 bytes) is a licence-carriage artifact under C-licence. check-repo.py::_third_party_provenance validates it against constants hardcoded IN THE CHECKER: expected_group_counts uupm-data=28 and uupm-python=3, coverage 'must be exactly 75 unique / 76 memberships', an expected_third_party set built from data/**/*.csv plus scripts/core.py, design_system.py, search.py on disk, plus per-file SHA-256, per-group treeSha256, a global coverage treeSha256 and a manifest self-hash that 'must occur exactly once'. Deleting 28 CSVs and 3 Python files removes 31 of the 75 covered files. tools/check-v3-docs.mjs (3,022 lines) re-implements the same validation with its own pins, and tools/test-product-flow.mjs asserts installed-bundle provenance. There is no build-provenance tool: grep for THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE across tools/ and bin/ returns only check-repo.py, check-v3-docs.mjs and test-product-flow.mjs — three readers, zero writers. The manifest must be regenerated by hand or by a new generator, and the hardcoded expectations must be edited in two places. The candidate budgets none of this and does not list the file as surviving.
fatalFlaws.evidence: tools/check-repo.py:288-620 (constants at :433-440, :528, :535-536, :559-560); tools/check-v3-docs.mjs:377,542-559,703-790; tools/test-product-flow.mjs:19; skills/sitesmith/THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json exists on disk, absent from the candidate's fileTree.

Do not edit' (line 137). It requires ASSET-MANIFEST.md, fails with 'no asset manifest' when absent (line 386-388), and its own error text points the reader at v2/25-assets.md and v2/24-asset-plan.md (lines 223, 388). The candidate deletes v2/, asset-plan.mjs and visual-assets.mjs while keeping the gate that enforces their output. Fifteen of gate-fixtures' production expectations still assert this behaviour. CI still needs the markdown mode for benchmarks/*/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md and benchmarks/*/site/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md (.github/workflows/verify.yml:83-100), so both modes must coexist.

The repo's only assignment-blinded review machinery is critique-gate.mjs plus tools/open-key.mjs and tools/test-open-key.mjs, with 14 fixtures under tests/gates/critique covering key-opened-early, reviewer-is-builder, edited-after-locking and so on. data/font-families.txt is an undisclosed derived work. Roughly 1,800 Google Fonts names can only come from data/google-fonts.csv, which is a ui-ux-pro-max MIT-covered file inside the uupm-data provenance group. Extracting a name column produces a new derived artifact that needs its own attribution and a provenance entry, while the candidate simultaneously deletes the source. The derivation is never stated.

The holdout plus two prototypes have to land as benchmark directories with committed diversity reports, not as ad-hoc builds, or A9 cannot be evaluated and _gallery_coverage will disagree with reality.

The candidate's own weakest point is understated. The token-naming thesis rests on n=2 and NORDRIG-AB-FORENSICS.md:126-129 says in terms that a thesis step is 'Not proven' to cause the win in general. The candidate turns that into a CI gate (vocabulary.mjs) whose only defence against gaming is a freeze at THESIS, which it admits does not stop a model that plans ahead.
overengineering: Three new lint scripts (tools/floor-lint.mjs, tools/state-fields-consumed.mjs, scripts/vocabulary.mjs) all gate authoring discipline over a package that a single maintainer writes. state-fields-consumed.mjs failing CI when an unread field is added to a schema consumed by exactly one skill is process for its own sake.

The 'three ways' section required in every floor file triples floor authoring cost, and floor-lint can only count three renditions — it cannot check they are visually unrelated, which is the entire claim. The mechanism the lint actually enforces is 'a heading exists and contains no hex codes'.

pick.mjs is a hash wrapper around a decision the model already made in thinking. It costs a script, a unit test, an override counter, a state field, a fixture, and the single most attackable line in the candidate's own risk section — to avoid the model writing 'I pick candidate 3'.

Four floor files plus a redesign overlay, where the nordrig evidence distinguishes exactly two layers (thesis versus craft floor, NORDRIG-AB-FORENSICS.md:141-144). floors/redesign.md as an overlay reinstates the second routing axis the candidate claims to have deleted, since REDESIGN is now a per-run condition rather than a per-surface verb.

The always-loaded control plane at ~1,900 tokens is 92% of the entire winning skill's budget spent on routing, passes, stop conditions, precedence and a scripts table — none of which frontend-design has, and none of which the one measurement in this repo shows buys design quality.
constraintViolations: C-licence / A5: the candidate's fileTree omits skills/sitesmith/THIRD-PARTY-PROVENANCE.json, a required licence-carriage artifact validated by check-repo.py, check-v3-docs.mjs and test-product-flow.mjs. It also omits scripts/package.json, which the installer and the clean-install CI job both read.

The candidate's distinction (it chooses among the model's own designs and authors none) is coherent but the script output IS the selection, and the candidate itself names this as the most attackable point.

The measuring tool (tools/context-budget.mjs) hardcodes the v2 paths, has no floors/ or stacks/ awareness, and never fails. As specified, A3 would be recorded from a number that does not measure the proposed architecture.

The candidate deletes critique-gate.mjs and open-key.mjs's consumer, the repo's only sealed blinded-review machinery, and offers 'write critique before re-reading own thesis' in its place under a no-sub-agents constraint and a zero paid-spend budget.

The control group still fails as required.
attacks.verdict:
Buildable, and the architecture is defensible — but the candidate costs its own delete list at zero, and the delete list is the single largest piece of work in the proposal.

WHAT SURVIVES in skills/sitesmith/: verify.mjs unchanged (it reads nothing from data/, v2/ or references/ — grep confirms zero external reads, so the control group at benchmarks/06-redesign/before/ keeps failing exactly as C-control-group requires); journey.mjs unchanged bar one string; production-gate.mjs unchanged but orphaned from its ASSET-MANIFEST.md authoring docs; references/ and references/impeccable/ verbatim; LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md. REWRITTEN, not renamed: stack-router.mjs (hard-binds data/stacks/*.csv, exits 2 without it, has no static adapter), direction-history.mjs (imports the deleted direction-record.mjs; one seed not two; fingerprint has luminance but no hue), token-drift.mjs (new state.json mode alongside the existing markdown-contract mode CI still needs), SKILL.md (complete). MOVED: portfolio-diversity.mjs to tools/, which orphans a link in docs/v3/ADOPTION-ARCHITECTURE.md:215. DELETED: 10 of 17 scripts, all 28 CSVs, all 18 v2/ files, all 24 blocks/ files, PIPELINE.json. Scripts kept: 7 of 17, and only 3 of those (verify, journey, production-gate) work as-is.

CHECK-REPO.PY: 11 of 17 checks pass, 6 break. Passing: SKILL.md line cap (249 < 500), reference-map line counts (vacuously — no such links remain), attribution headers, change notices, TOC rule, LICENSE, Apache licence hash, skill notices, plugin manifests, gallery assets, gallery coverage.
